sentences.text: This reference made by the respondent No.1/SLAO, KIADB (Metro Rail Project), Bengaluru under Sections 30 and 31(2) of L.A. Act, 1894 (L.A. Act, 1894 for short), for apportionment of compensation amount.

.2. As per the records, the respondent No.1 has acquired the property measuring 98.33 Sq. Meters in Sy.No.30/1A of Yalachenahalli village for the purpose of BMRCL under Preliminary Notification dated 31.01.2009 and Final Notification dated 01.01.2010.
The award passed on 05.03.2012, fixing compensation of Rs.51,82,794/- in this case.
As there is pendency L.A.C. No.54/2012 of the suit, the L.A.O. has referred the matter to this Court and has deposited a sum of Rs.46,64,514 /- after deducting Income tax.
The said amount has been kept in F.D. in the Syndicate Bank, Market Branch, Bengaluru.
.3. After receipt of reference, this Court issued notice to both parties.
In pursuance of the notice, the claimants 1 and 2 and respondents 1 and 2 had entered appearance.

.4. The claimant No.1 Chinnatayappa filed claim statement stating that the land bearing Sy. No.
30/1A to an extent of 98.33 Sq. Meters of Yalachenahalli village has been acquired by KIADB for formation of Metro Rail Works (BMRCL).

Further stated that the BMRCL passed meager compensation and in the said area, the market value of the property is Rs.7,000/- per Sq. feet.
Further stated that he is entitled for the market value together with interest @ 24% p.a. with accrued thereof from the date of acquiring the land by BMRCL.

Further stated that the said L.A.C.
No.54/2012 authority not properly assessed, verified the market value of the property in the said locality and they have passed an award only Rs.4,595/- per Sq. feet instead of Rs. 7,000/- per Sq.
feet.
Except himself, there are no other persons have any right, title and interest over the acquired property.
Hence, he is entitled for entire award amount.

.5. The claimant No.2 V. Nagaraju has filed claim statement stating that the respondent No.2 took the possession of the property bearing Sy. No.30/1A of Yalachenahalli village by awarding the amount of Rs.41,64,514/- towards compensation.

The claimant No.2 had filed detailed objection not to release the compensation amount in favour of any alleged claimants including the claimant No.1 in this case, as there is a partition suit which is pending between claimants 1 and 2 along with other claimants since 2007.

The claimant No.2 filed all the documents with relating to the suit pending L.A.C. No.54/2012 between joint family members in O.S. No.1824/2007 and hence, the respondent No.2 has not disbursed the awarded amount along with other benefits.

The said amount of Rs.
41,64,514/- had deposited in the Bank of India, Market branch, Bengaluru.
Further stated that his mother is also one of the coparcener and daughter of late. Muniswamappa.
Thereafter, the mother of claimant No.2 has passed away and hence, the claimant No.2 is claiming his notional share out of the awarded amount along with other properties.

2 .6.

Further, the claimant No.2 stated that the grand father of the claimant No.2 has acquired the acquired portion through their ancestors/self acquired and his grand father had 9 children and out of them, his mother was second daughter of late.
Muniswamappa and thereafter, he came to know that the said Muniswamappa had bequeathed his self acquired properties in favour of his daughters.

Further stated that without consent and knowledge of his mother, the male L.A.C. No.54/2012 children i.e., Narayanappa, Srinivas and Chinnathayappa got divided the properties which belongs to late. Muniswamappa, who is grand father of claimant No.2 without making claimant No.2 as party in the partition and also without giving their legitimate share and hence, the claimant No.2 and his two brothers have filed the suit in O.S. No. 1824/2007, which is pending.

In the said suit,
the claimant No.1 along with his children appeared and filed their objections by denying the rights of claimant No.2.
Further the claimant No.2 submits that he is also entitled to claim his mother's share along with his brothers.
In view of the above said facts and circumstances, the claimant No.2 along with other children of late. Chinnamma are claiming 1/9th share in the remaining properties of late.
Muniswamappa and they are entitled for 1/9th share in the award amount along with other benefits given by KIADB.
Hence, he is entitled for award amount.

In order to prove their case, the GPA holder of claimant No.1 is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 25.
.8.

On the basis of the above, the points for consideration are that:
1) Whether the claimant No.1 proves that he is the absolute owner of the acquired property and entitled for the compensation?
2) Whether the claimant No.2 proves that he is the absolute owner of the acquired property and entitled for the compensation?
3) What order or award?

.9. Heard the arguments, perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1: In the affirmative Point No.1: In the negative Point No.3: As per final order, for the following:
L.A.C. No.54/2012 REASONS .10.
Points 1 and 2: Both points are interlinked with each other, hence, taken together for discussion, for convenience, also to avoid repetition of facts.
This is a reference filed under Sections 30 and 31 of L.A. Act for apportionment of compensation as well as to decide the title of rival claimants regarding acquired property.

.11. The case made out by the claimant No.1 Chinnatayappa in his claim statement as well as evidence affidavit in nutshell is that originally the property involved in this case belongs to the grand father of claimant No.1 Muniswamappa @ Pillappa who Chinnathayappa vs Spl Lao on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32966307/
3 had 3 sons and during the life time of said Muniswamappa, there was a partition of the joint family properties under a partition deed dated 16.07.1962.
In the said partition, the property in Sy. No.30/1, 30/4 and 31/1 totally measuring 1 acre 34 guntas of land fallen to the share of father of claimant No.1 namely Muniswamappa.

Thereafter, there was another partition in the L.A.C. No.54/2012 family of father of claimant No.1 Muniswamappa as on 08.01.1981 and in the said partition, 'D' schedule property fallen to the share of claimant No.1 Chinnatayappa i.e., property bearing Sy. No. 30/1A measuring 15 guntas and Sy.
No. 30/2 measuring 1 acre 3 guntas of land.

It is also made out by the claimant No.1 that father of claimant No.1 executed a Will dated 21.12.1992 and in the said registered Will 'D' schedule property fallen to the share of claimant No.1 to an extent of 5  guntas of land in Sy. No. 30/1B and Sy. No.
31/1D.
Accordingly, the claimant No.1 claims exclusive right over the acquired property and the claimant No.2 has no right over the said property.
.12. The case made out by the claimant No.2 V. Nagaraju in his claim statement is that his mother and claimant No.1 are children of Muniswamappa and they are coparceners.
Accordingly, the suit has been filed in O.S.No.1824/2007 for partition of the joint family properties on the file of CCH-7 and the said suit is L.A.C. No.54/2012 pending for disposal.

Accordingly, claimed that the claimant No.2 V. Nagaraju being grand son of Muniswamappa and nephew of claimant No.1 is entitled for equal share in the compensation awarded in respect of acquired property involved in this case.

With these backgrounds, the materials placed before the Court has to be appreciated and the Court has to consider whether claimant No.2 has undivided right or whether claimant No.1 has acquired valid right and title over the property as per the documents claimed by him in his evidence affidavit.
.13. The son of claimant No.1 who is the GPA holder of claimant No.1 has been examined as PW.1 on behalf of the claimant No.1.
PW.1 in his evidence affidavit stated in consonance with the claim made by the claimant No.1 in this case claiming absolute owner of the acquired property.
The claimant No.1 also produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.25.
Ex . P.1
is the GPA executed by claimant No.1 in favour of PW.1 who is his son.
L.A.C. No.54/2012 Ex.P.2 to 9, 16 and 17 are the encumbrance certificates in respect of the property involved in this case.
Ex.P.10 is the Will executed by father of claimant No.1 Muniswamappa as on 21.12.1992.
Ex . P.13
is the RTC extract of the acquired land.
Ex . P.14
is the registered declaration executed by claimant No.1.
Ex. P.15
is the tax paid receipt.
Ex . P.18
is the partition deed dated 16.07.1962.
Ex . P.19
is the certified copy of the order sheet in O.S.No.1824/2007.
Ex.P.20 to 24 are the plaint, amended plaints, written statement in O.S.No.1824/2007.
Ex . P.25
is the Will.
.14. Based on the aforesaid documents, the claimant No.1 claimed that he has proved his title over the acquired land.
As discussed earlier, the claimant No.1 claims that the property was originally belongs to their grand father Muniswamappa and he has executed a registered partition deed as on 16.07.1962.
To substantiate the said fact, the claimant No.1 produced certified copy of the said partition deed at Ex.P.18 along L.A.C. No.54/2012 with typed copy at Ex.P.18(a).
In the said partition, 'C' schedule property has been allotted to the share of father of claimant No.1 namely Muniswamappa.

The said schedule discloses about allotment of property to the share of father of Chinnathayappa vs Spl Lao on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32966307/
4 claimant No.1 Muniswamappa in Sy. No.30/1, 30/4 and 31/1 totally measuring 1 acre 34 guntas of Yalachenahalli village.
Therefore, allotment of property to the father of claimant No.1 in the partition deed of the year 1962 has been proved by the claimant No.1 and the said partition is not in dispute in this case.
.15. Further case made out by the claimant No.1 is that his father executed a registered Will on 21.12.1992 and in the said Will, 'D' schedule property has been bequeathed in favour of claimant No.1.
The certified copy of the said Will has been produced at Ex.P.10.

In the said Will at Ex.P.10,
Muniswamappa has given the properties to his sons and excluded his daughters from the property by assigning the reasons that he has L.A.C. No.54/2012 performed the marriage of his daughters and whatever to be given to the daughters has been given to them during their marriage.

Therefore,
in the Will, said Muniswamappa has given the reasons why he has excluded his daughters from the properties.
Admittedly, the claimant No.2 is the grand son of said Muniswamappa.

The said Muniswamappa during his life time itself by executing the Will excluded the mother of claimant No.2 by giving reason that he has performed the marriage of his daughters and whatever to be given to his daughters has been given to them during their marriage.
The execution of Will also not seriously disputed by the claimant No.2 during the cross-examination of PW.1.
Hence, it is clear that the claimant No.1 has proved the execution of Will by his father in respect of the acquired property that has been involved in this case.

Apart from that, the Will has been acted upon and the properties have been mutated on the basis of the said Will that is evident from the L.A.C. No.54/2012 entries found in the mutation register extracts as well as RTC extracts.
.16.
The claim of the claimant No.2 is that he had undivided right over the acquired property and he has filed the suit in O.S.No.1824/2007 for partition.
Now it is found that the said suit has been dismissed for non-prosecution as on 06.11.2023.
The learned advocate for the claimant No.1 produced certified copy of the order sheet in O.S.No.1824/2007 along with a memo as on 09.02.2024.
The said fact is not in dispute by the respondents or claimant No.2.

Apart from that the claimant No.2 also not chosen to complete cross-examination of PW.1 nor chosen to step into the witness box to give any rebuttal evidence or to substantiate his claim over the acquired property involved in this case.
Therefore, there is no material on record to show that the claimant No.2 had any right over the acquired property.
The acquired property belongs to the claimant No.1 is also not in dispute and it is also not in dispute L.A.C. No.54/2012
that '
D ' schedule property in the Will has been acquired by claimant No.1 on the basis of aforesaid Will

. In the absence of any rebuttal evidence or any materials placed before the Court to show that claimant No.2 and his mother had any right over the properties, certainly it cannot be accepted that claimant No.2 has any right over the property involved in this case.
Meantime, the claimant No.1 has proved his title over the property.
Accordingly, the claimant No.1 is entitled for compensation.
Accordingly, I answer point No. 1 in the affirmative and point No. 2 in the negative.
.17. Point No.3:

In view of my findings on the above points 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

The reference made under Sections 30 and 31(2) of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894 is hereby partly allowed.

No.30/1A measuring 98.33 Sq. Meters of Yalachenahalli village along with statutory benefits.

The above claimant No.1 shall has to execute an indemnity bond with one surety,
undertaking to re-deposit the compensation amount either in this court or in any other court, if ordered to do so, which amount he is going to receive in these case.
